subject: general
question:
In a certain code language, the letters of the English alphabet are coded as per their alphabetical order (A as 1 and Z as 26). However, if a vowel is immediately preceded as well as immediately followed by a consonant, its code would be 99.

What will be the code for 'BLAST' in this language?
solution:
The logic followed here is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6b07fd0557c31540782a37b7252c5fb9387bfc2d7d3dd19f34eea3a5f0b7f9c.png] 

According to the alphabetical positions of the letters,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd52b1a21a0d1579aa73090cd58c4cc135c5171adc276c99c1569ff1f14e386e.png] 

 
• If a vowel is immediately preceded as well as immediately followed by a consonant, its code would be 99. So, A is coded as 99.
 
• The remaining letters of the English alphabet are coded as per their alphabetical order

Hence, ‘**212991920**’ is the correct answer.
